Chapter Details: Comparable indicators on energy, connectivity and data storage. 27 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
revision_notes: World Bank indicators EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS and EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS give Gabon's urban electricity access as 99.2% and rural access as 29.0% for 2023, a gap of 70.2 percentage points. This exceeds 60pp, so the correct code is 1 (Gap >60pp), not 2 (41-60pp) as originally scored; the cited comments already noted a ~65pp gap, which was itself inconsistent with a code of 2. Figures cross-checked across TradingEconomics and CountryDataHub, both sourcing World Bank Open Data (2023 vintage); the Energypedia source cited previously had no usable current urban figure.
revised_comments: Gabon has a wide urban-rural electrification gap. World Bank data for 2023 put electricity access at 99.2% of the urban population against 29.0% of the rural population, a gap of roughly 70 percentage points, reflecting the concentration of grid electricity supply in Libreville and other urban centres relative to rural areas.
